sections.heading: Why observability
sections.content: Without visibility into prompts, latencies, tokens and errors, AI systems drift in quality and cost. Observability adds logs, metrics and evaluations to keep systems reliable and affordable.

sections.caption: Core metrics: p50/p95 latency, input/output tokens, cost, error/refusal rate, evaluation pass rate.

sections.heading: Metrics to collect
content: Input/Output tokens per call (and rolling average)
Estimated cost per call and per user/session
Evaluation pass rate on a fixed test set

sections.heading: Logging wrapper (JS)
Cost estimation
sections.explainer: Multiply input and output tokens by the per‑token price on each side. Use this to set per‑task budgets and choose models.

sections.heading: Hands‑on (Run Test + API Config)
sections.description: Measure latency and tokens on 3 prompts. Then switch models and compare cost/latency.
steps: Open Run Test and create 3 cases with expected outputs
Use a budget model and record latency and tokens
Switch to a higher‑quality model and repeat
Compare accuracy (tests), latency and estimated cost
Decide a policy: when should each model be used?
